name: IL-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 5 points on the partisan baseline
Melissa Bean has outraised Jennifer Davis and drawn about $5.5 million in outside support
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot removes Krishnamoorthi's personal advantage
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point to a Democratic hold: a D+5 district, a favorable national environment, and Bean's clear fundraising and outside-spending edge, with markets pricing her near 95%. The open-seat status and absence of any public polling argue for trimming a few points off the fundamentals-based margin rather than treating it as fully safe.
model.watch: Any late public polling or a surge of Republican outside spending into the open seat would be the clearest signal of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Raja Krishnamoorthi (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Raja Krishnamoorthi's retirement leaves an open Democratic-held seat in the Chicago suburbs with a 5-point Democratic partisan lean. Melissa Bean, a former congresswoman, has raised about $2.4 million and benefits from roughly $5.5 million in outside support, while Republican Jennifer Davis has raised about $1.7 million with little outside help.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price the Democratic side near 95%. The race is rated Likely Democratic, with the open-seat nature the main reason it is not placed in the safe column.
